title: Researcher asks Walter Lewis about Stormy Weather and the Tulane and Broad record
summary: The interviewer explains how he traced Stormy Weather's Jackson, Mississippi records to New Orleans; Walter Lewis knows him only by nickname as a boogie-woogie blues player.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: I got it on tape and my Californian friend and I listened to this record, just listened to the music and the lyrics sounded so interesting. He was thinking about sitting in a jail or so. And he said they built up a new jail on Tulane and Broad. And we didn't know anything about them. These records were made in Jackson, Mississippi. But Tulane, Broad is just a common name for a spree, but Tulane sounded very much like New Orleans. And we got out the map and found this criminal. Tulane and Broad. Tulane and Broad. The Paris prison. Yeah. And so I wrote to Dick Allen, the curator of the archives of New Orleans Church, if he knew anything about it. He wrote back that he knew him. And now he knew him too. What else do you know? Do you know his real name?

No, let me see. I don't know what his real name was. That was his nickname. A lot of them guys just knew him about his nickname. You don't know his real name. I don't know what his real name was. But they used to call him Stormy Weather. He used to boogie woogie. He used to love to play the boogie when he'd sing all the little rally blues, you know? Yeah. I don't know too much about him, but outside of, you know, I didn't know anything personal about him. Outside of, we'd get together and have a little ball and get drunk and, you know, like that.
Do you think he was from New Orleans? Yeah, he was. He was from New Orleans. Maybe, uh, it took, uh, tell me more about him.
